source.title: Sparsified Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Interpretable Quantum State Tomography
source.authors: Xing Wu; Hua-Xin Wang; Jia-Ju Liu; Rui-Qing He; Jian-Dong Shang; Heng-Liang Guo; Qiang Chen

record.tranche_reason: The study includes a random-label control, but it measures whether Pauli-support and hidden-alignment signals survive shuffled input–target pairing. It does not measure whether the network fits random labels or its training or test error on them.
record.gate_note: The random-label control is recorded as a related result under fits_no_version: its metrics measure support recovery and hidden alignment, not the random-label fitting behavior in V1. No results test V2–V6.
record.test_reason: The random-label control measures Pauli-support recovery and hidden-representation alignment, not training-set fit, prediction error on random targets, or learning dynamics. Its results therefore do not test V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' interpretation of the random-label control: channel preference and GHZ-aligned hidden representations depend on the physical input–target relation rather than dataset-specific shortcuts. This conclusion concerns structural inspection in the controlled GHZ benchmark, not whether the KAN can memorize random targets.
record.recipe_differences: The random-label control shuffles training input–target pairing and evaluates support recovery and hidden alignment; it does not test image classification or random-label fitting error.

fits_no_version.finding: At 1000 shots across ten seeds, shuffled training input–target pairing reduces top-12 support Jaccard from 1.000 ± 0.000 to 0.026 ± 0.030 and held-out hidden-probe R2 from 0.9985 ± 0.0007 to 0.0034 ± 0.0129.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this GHZ-subspace tomography benchmark, recovery of physical Pauli support and linearly accessible GHZ variables depends on the training input–target relation.

record.code_released: The code will be made available in a public repository upon publication; no URL is stated.
record.problems: The random-label control reports support-recovery and hidden-probe metrics rather than training error or random-label test error, so it cannot establish the random-label fitting claim.
record.rows_left_out: No other results bear on the claim versions. The remaining experiments concern GHZ-subspace tomography, Pauli support, pathways, hidden representations, formula recovery, noise stability, or off-manifold behavior.

untested.parts: Random-label training error, chance-level test performance, and fitting with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Perfect training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs. Appended Gaussian decoy channels do not test this.
Training fit and test error across fractions of randomly corrupted labels. Measurement noise and depolarizing attenuation are different interventions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels; no relevant training trajectories are reported.

record.verdict_notes: Near-zero held-out hidden-probe R2 is compatible with either successful or unsuccessful memorization of shuffled training targets; it cannot support or challenge random-label fitting.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report training error or test error after training on random labels.
No comparison of training time or convergence across true and corrupted labels.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input fitting experiment.
No sweep over fractions of randomly corrupted labels measuring training fit and test error.
No test of weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, or their removal on random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
No analysis of whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: sparsified KAN
rows.size_stated: 63 input channels, six hidden units, and three output variables
rows.operation_detail: Training input–target pairing shuffled; evaluation performed on unshuffled held-out data.
rows.measure: Top-12 extended-channel Jaccard; hidden-subspace probe R2
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± SD across 10 seeds, as stated.
rows.note: Measures collapse of channel-support recovery and hidden-subspace alignment under shuffled pairing, not training-set fit or test error.
rows.check: The values and conditions match Section III.E and Table S7. Neither metric establishes whether random targets were memorized. Split the Jaccard and hidden-probe R2 measurements into separate rows to follow the one-measure-per-row rule.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
